Title: Spine and the day-one proof
Description: One thin vertical thread proven end to end before any feature work.

Title: Repository skeleton and typed settings
Description: The module layout of SRC-001 3.1 with a typed settings loader that fails fast.
AcceptanceCriteria: `app/modules/{auth,users,expenses,categories,receipts,admin}/` each contain router.py, service.py, repository.py, schemas.py, models.py | `app/core/` exists; there is NO package named `platform` anywhere in the tree | starting with a required env var removed exits non-zero before binding the port, and prints the missing key by name | `.env.example` lists every variable the settings class reads - asserted by a test that imports the class and diffs the two

Title: Two database roles, verified against the catalog
Description: An owner role that migrates and a runtime role that cannot escape row security.
AcceptanceCriteria: querying pg_roles for the runtime role returns rolsuper=false and rolbypassrls=false | querying pg_class for every protected table returns relowner != the runtime role | querying pg_class returns relforcerowsecurity=true for expenses, categories, sessions | startup aborts with a named error when any of the three assertions fails - proved by pointing DATABASE_URL at the owner role and observing the abort

Title: Baseline migration and row-level security
Description: The first Alembic revision, with policies covering every command.
AcceptanceCriteria: `alembic upgrade head` exits 0 against an EMPTY database | running it a second time exits 0 and changes nothing | migrate down then up again exits 0 | every protected table has a FOR ALL policy with BOTH `USING` and `WITH CHECK`, verified by querying pg_policies | the migration runs under pg_advisory_xact_lock - proved by holding the lock in a second session and observing the migration block, then time out

Title: Seed: two people with known amounts
Description: The fixture the gate computes against. Under the test tree, never in the image.
AcceptanceCriteria: seeding an empty test database creates exactly 2 people, each with 8 categories | person A has exactly the four expenses of P-UND-02: 125000, 34050, 210000, 9999 paise on 2026-08-01/03/03/05 | running the seed twice from empty produces identical row counts - printed and compared | the seed script is absent from the built image - asserted by listing the image contents | the seed refuses to run against any database not named spendwise_test

Title: Register and sign in, end to end in a real browser
Description: The exact path a person walks, not an API call that skips the interface.
AcceptanceCriteria: through a real browser session, person A registers and lands on the dashboard | the session cookie is OBSERVED in the response headers to be httpOnly and SameSite=Lax | signing out then replaying the old cookie returns 401 | an unauthenticated request to /api/expenses returns 401 and no data in the body

Title: Person A creates and reads one expense
Description: One record, owned, readable back through the application.
AcceptanceCriteria: as A, POST /api/expenses creates a row; the row in the database carries A's user_id | as A, GET returns it | submitting a forged user_id, a forged id and a forged total in the body has no effect on the stored row

Title: THE GATE: person B is denied, at the database layer
AcceptanceCriteria: as B, GET /api/expenses/{A's id} returns 404 - not 403, and identical to a nonexistent id | as the RUNTIME role with app.user_id set to B, `SELECT * FROM expenses WHERE id = {A's id}` returns ZERO rows | as B, UPDATE of A's expense affects zero rows | as B, DELETE of A's expense affects zero rows | as B, INSERT of a row carrying A's user_id is REJECTED by the WITH CHECK clause | as B, the list endpoint returns exactly B's seeded count and no row of A's | inserting an expense under B pointing at a category owned by A is REJECTED by the composite foreign key

Title: RED-PROOF the gate
Description: A gate nobody has watched fail is decoration.
AcceptanceCriteria: in a scratch copy, `ALTER TABLE expenses NO FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` is applied and the change is confirmed to be a real change | E0-S7's database-layer assertion is re-run and OBSERVED FAILING - the row comes back | the change is reverted and the revert is verified by re-querying pg_class | E0-S7 passes again | all four observations are pasted into the evidence record, not summarised

Title: THE GATE: the business rule computes 75810
Description: Computed by the application from seeded rows, not by a fixture asserting on itself.
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/expenses/summary?from=2026-08-01&to=2026-08-31 with today mocked to 2026-08-05 returns daily_average_paise = 75810 | the same call returns total_paise = 379049 and count = 4 | the value is produced by application code reading the database - proved by changing a seeded amount and observing the average change | the breakdown sums exactly to total_paise | the day series contains 31 rows, including days with zero spending

Title: Health, readiness and the clean-clone evidence record
Description: The witness. Four lines, not one.
AcceptanceCriteria: /healthz returns 200 with no body and without touching the database | /readyz returns status, revision and build when EXPOSE_VERSION is set | the whole of E0-S1..S9 runs from a FRESH git clone into an empty directory with a brand-new virtualenv and the test database dropped and rebuilt from empty | the evidence record carries FOUR separate lines: J1-SUBSTITUTE-A observed, J1-SUBSTITUTE-B open, J1 open, J2 open - never collapsed into one tick | a NAMED human is recorded as having watched it, with date and time

Title: Password policy and bcrypt off the event loop
AcceptanceCriteria: a password of 11 characters is rejected with 422 | a password of 12 is accepted | a password of 73 bytes UTF-8 is rejected with 422 | bcrypt runs in a threadpool - proved by issuing 5 concurrent sign-ins and observing an unrelated GET complete in under 200ms | sign-in with an unknown email takes within 20% of the time of a known email over 50 samples

Title: Duplicate email and case-insensitive identity
AcceptanceCriteria: registering an existing email returns 409 with code EMAIL_TAKEN | registering `A@x.com` when `a@x.com` exists returns 409 | the stored email preserves the capitalisation typed

Title: Session lifetimes and the throttled heartbeat
AcceptanceCriteria: a session older than 30 days is rejected regardless of activity | a `user` session idle 14 days + 1 minute is rejected; 13 days is accepted | an `admin` session idle 31 minutes is rejected; 29 minutes is accepted | last_seen_at is written at most once per minute - proved by 10 requests in 10 seconds producing exactly one UPDATE

Title: First-administrator bootstrap
AcceptanceCriteria: with zero admins and BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_EMAIL set, that address registering becomes admin | with zero admins and a DIFFERENT address registering, they become `user` | with one admin already present, the bootstrap address registering becomes `user` | with zero admins and the variable unset, the application exits non-zero at startup

Title: Reset codes: issue and redeem
AcceptanceCriteria: an issued code is stored only as a SHA-256 hash - the plaintext appears in no row | redeeming it once succeeds; redeeming the same code again returns the ALREADY_USED outcome | a code older than one hour returns the EXPIRED outcome, distinct from ALREADY_USED and from NOT_RECOGNISED | issuing a second code invalidates the first in the same transaction | on successful redemption every session of that person has revoked_at set, in the same transaction

Title: Rate limits, with numbers
AcceptanceCriteria: the 11th sign-in attempt in a minute from one IP returns 429 with a Retry-After header | the 11th sign-in attempt in a minute against one email from DIFFERENT IPs returns 429 | the 6th registration in a minute from one IP returns 429 | the 7th reset redemption in a minute from one IP returns 429 | each configured value is half its stated effective value, and a test asserts the arithmetic against the worker count

Title: Current user, and the receipts feature flag
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/auth/me returns id, email, display_name and role for the signed-in person | it returns receipts_enabled=false when no storage bucket is configured, true when one is | it never returns password_hash - asserted by introspecting the response model, not by reading the JSON

Title: The error envelope
AcceptanceCriteria: every non-2xx response body matches {error:{code,message,field?}} - asserted across every endpoint by a test that walks the route table | a validation failure reports `field` using the client's field name (`amount`), never the converted one (`amount_paise`) | the framework's default validation body never reaches a client

Title: Expense validation
AcceptanceCriteria: an amount of 0 is rejected 422; -1 is rejected 422 | an amount with three decimal places is rejected 422 and is NOT rounded | an amount above 10^12 paise is rejected 422 | spent_on more than 1 year ahead is rejected 422; more than 10 years back is rejected 422 | a description of 501 characters is rejected 422; a whitespace-only description is stored as NULL

Title: Category ownership enforced by the database
AcceptanceCriteria: creating an expense with another person's category_id is rejected by the composite foreign key, not by application code alone - proved by attempting the INSERT directly as the runtime role | two categories with the same name differing only in case are rejected 409 for the same person | two people may each have a category named Groceries

Title: Category delete nulls, never deletes
AcceptanceCriteria: deleting a category sets category_id to NULL on every expense that used it | the expense count before and after the delete is identical | the confirm text names the exact count of affected expenses

Title: Category rename and recolour
AcceptanceCriteria: renaming a category leaves every expense's category_id unchanged | renaming to an existing name (any case) returns 409 | recolouring to a value not matching ^#[0-9a-f]{6}$ returns 422

Title: The summary endpoint
AcceptanceCriteria: one request returns total, count, average, breakdown and the day series | the day series has exactly (to - from + 1) rows, including zero days | the breakdown sums exactly to the total - asserted, not eyeballed | an Uncategorised bucket appears when null-category spending exists, ordered LAST | SUM() is cast back to an integer - a Decimal never reaches the response model

Title: The daily-average formula
AcceptanceCriteria: for the seeded fixture with today = 2026-08-05, the average is exactly 75810 | for a range wholly in the past, the average uses the full span and does not change on a later day | for a range wholly in the future, the average is null and the endpoint returns 200 - not a 500 | rounding is half-up: a total of 3 paise over 2 elapsed days returns 2, not 1

Title: Range validation and ordering
AcceptanceCriteria: from > to returns 422 | a span of 401 days returns 422 naming the cap | two expenses on the same date return in a stable order across 10 identical requests | the list is ordered spent_on DESC, created_at DESC, id DESC

Title: Update and delete an expense
AcceptanceCriteria: PATCH changes amount, date, description and category; it does NOT change owner, id or created_at | PATCH re-runs every validation of E2-S1 - a three-decimal amount is rejected on update too | DELETE removes the row and, when a receipt is attached, deletes the object AFTER the row commits | PATCH or DELETE against another person's expense returns 404, identical to a nonexistent id | (the update ENDPOINT exists in v1; no screen does - SRC-001 section 14)

Title: The dashboard
Description: What a person actually looks at.

Title: Design tokens lifted into the client
AcceptanceCriteria: tokens.css is imported by the client build and no component declares a raw hex - asserted by a grep over the source | every number renders through one shared en-IN formatter - asserted by a grep for toLocaleString outside it | the focus rule is declared exactly once

Title: Period picker and URL state
AcceptanceCriteria: selecting `This month` sets from/to in the query string to the first and last day of the current month in Asia/Kolkata | reloading the page preserves the period | the browser back button returns to the previous period rather than leaving the app

Title: The category ribbon as a real control
AcceptanceCriteria: one Tab press moves focus to the ribbon; a second Tab leaves it (roving tabindex) | Left and Right arrows move between bands; Home and End jump to first and last | Enter toggles the filter; Escape clears it | each band's accessible name contains the category, the amount and the percentage | the selected band is distinguishable with colour rendering disabled - two cues, asserted by a grayscale screenshot diff | band widths are exact fractions of the total; printed percentages sum to exactly 100

Title: Filtering re-scopes the right things
AcceptanceCriteria: selecting a band changes the total, count, average, day bars and list | selecting a band does NOT change the ribbon's own proportions | the per-day subtotals shown beneath the total sum exactly to the displayed total

Title: The add-expense panel
AcceptanceCriteria: focus is trapped while open and restored to the trigger on close | Escape closes; the background is inert | a dirty form confirms before discarding | the submit control disables on first click and stays disabled until the response settles | the entry does NOT appear in the list before the server confirms it

Title: Screen states
AcceptanceCriteria: a brand-new account sees the first-run state: no ribbon, no bars, one primary action | a filter matching nothing shows a DIFFERENT state, with a clear-filter affordance | a failed summary request shows an error panel with retry that preserves the period - and NEVER renders 0.00 | under prefers-reduced-motion the panel appears with no transition - asserted by measuring transition-duration

Title: Session ending mid-use
AcceptanceCriteria: a 401 on any request routes to sign-in with a reason banner | two concurrent 401s produce exactly ONE redirect | a half-typed expense survives in memory across the redirect

Title: Phone width
AcceptanceCriteria: at 375px wide there is no horizontal scroll on any screen | the panel enters from the bottom rather than the right | every interactive target is at least 44x44 CSS px

Title: Administration
Description: Keeping accounts working, without seeing money.

Title: require_admin applied once
AcceptanceCriteria: every /api/admin/* route is refused with 403 for a `user` - asserted by walking the route table, not by listing routes by hand | the check is declared once as a router dependency - asserted by a grep finding no per-handler role check | a `user` navigating to /admin sees a no-access screen, not the admin shell

Title: The admin response models cannot carry money
AcceptanceCriteria: no admin response model declares a field capable of holding an amount or a description - asserted by introspecting the Pydantic models | the session list model declares no ip and no user_agent field | NO policy on expenses or categories consults app.is_admin - asserted by querying pg_policies | admin_expense_stats() returns exactly two columns, expense_count and last_activity, and no column capable of holding an amount

Title: Reset, revoke, deactivate
AcceptanceCriteria: issuing a reset revokes every session of the target in the same transaction | deactivating refuses sign-in with the SAME generic 401 as a wrong password | a deactivated person's in-flight session is refused with ACCOUNT_DEACTIVATED | reactivating does not restore any revoked session

Title: Role change and the last-administrator guard
AcceptanceCriteria: demoting revokes every session of the target in the same transaction | promoting does not revoke sessions, and the new role applies on the very next request | demoting the last admin returns 409 | deactivating the last admin returns 409 | an admin issuing a reset against another admin returns 403 | an admin issuing a reset against themselves succeeds

Title: The audit record
AcceptanceCriteria: every admin mutation writes exactly one row in the same transaction | a forced failure of the audit write rolls back the change - proved by planting a constraint violation | reading the user list, the session list, or the audit view each writes one read-audit row | an action type not on the nine-item allowlist is rejected before the write | no audit row contains a token, an amount, a description or a receipt key - asserted by scanning every row after a full admin exercise | UPDATE and DELETE against the audit table are refused at the database

Title: Listing accounts and reading the record
AcceptanceCriteria: GET /api/admin/users paginates and searches by email and display name | the response carries no amount and no description for any person - asserted against the model | GET /api/admin/audit paginates newest-first and renders each row as a formatted sentence, never raw JSON | reading either endpoint writes exactly one read-audit row

Title: Receipts
Description: Optional, owner-only, never through the container.

Title: Upload via presigned POST
AcceptanceCriteria: the upload authorisation returns a POST policy asserting content-length-range and an allowed content type | uploading a 10MB+1 byte file is rejected BY STORAGE, not by the application | uploading text/html is rejected by the policy | the object carries Content-Disposition: attachment

Title: Attach, view, replace, remove
AcceptanceCriteria: attach refuses a staging key whose prefix does not match the caller | the view URL is resolved from the caller's own expense row - a key supplied in the request is ignored | an admin calling any receipt endpoint for another person receives 404 | replacing commits the row before deleting the previous object

Title: Graceful absence
AcceptanceCriteria: with no bucket configured, /api/auth/me reports receipts_enabled=false | the receipt control is not rendered when it is false | one WARN line at startup names the disabled feature

Title: Hardening
Description: Prove the checks can fail, and that nothing leaks.

Title: The log deny-list, red-proofed
AcceptanceCriteria: a reset code is planted through the real issue path and does NOT appear in captured stdout | a password is planted through the real sign-in path and does NOT appear | the database URL and signing secret do not appear in any startup line | each planted value is confirmed to have been genuinely present in the request before the assertion

Title: Secret rotation revokes everything
AcceptanceCriteria: changing JWT_SECRET and restarting revokes every live session at boot | the fingerprint row is updated and one INFO line reports the count | restarting again with the same secret revokes nothing

Title: The full negative suite passes
AcceptanceCriteria: every case in 09 NegativeTesting executes and passes | every endpoint has at least one cross-person case | a case that cannot be executed is reported as a FAILURE, never as an omission

Title: The day-one gate still passes
AcceptanceCriteria: E0-S7, E0-S8 and E0-S9 are re-run against the finished application and pass unchanged | the red-proof of E0-S8 is repeated and observed failing again

Title: Capabilities that must NOT exist
AcceptanceCriteria: no route, handler or CLI path hard-deletes a user - asserted by walking the route table and by the absence of a DELETE grant on users; DELETE /api/auth/me is SOFT (SW-ADR-150) and every row survives | no endpoint lets a person change their own email (SW-ADR-148 C narrowed this clause: display name and password are self-service by design) | both absences are proved by a NEGATIVE test that fails if the capability ever appears | (a specification that something does not exist still needs a test, or it silently arrives later)
